production.note: US model years. KBB's California listing links model years 2009 to 2018; its 2015 page is headed 'Used 2015 Ferrari California' with the trim 'T Convertible 2D' (kbb-california-2015) and its 2018 car is the 'California T Convertible 2D', while 'years 2014 and 2013 are know as California 30'. Revealed at Geneva in March 2014 (justcars-californiat); the Australian launch was in 2014 (carshowroom-californiat). The earlier naturally aspirated California is a separate car. Body: the owner confirmed on 5 October 2026 that 'Convertible' is right for the California T (2+2 with a folding hard-top, no coupe version).

body.note: KBB: trim 'T Convertible 2D' (kbb-california-2015); Top Gear: '2dr' (topgear-californiat-spec). A 2+2 with a folding hard top and no fixed-roof version. 'Convertible' is used because the guide's 'Roadster' is defined as a two-seat car; see reviewNotes.

configuration.note: Ferrari specification as printed by Just Cars: 'direct-injection 90 V8'

displacementL.note: 3,855 cc. Just Cars: '3,855 cc'; Top Gear: 'Engine Capacity: 3,855cc' (topgear-californiat-spec); Asphalte.ch: 'Displacement is 3855 cm3' (asphalte-californiat).

transmission.note: Ferrari specification table as printed by CarShowroom: 'F1, dual clutch 7 gears + Reverse'; Just Cars: 'F1-style 7-speed dual-clutch'. No manual was offered.

powerHp.note: Ferrari's rating is metric: 560 cv x 0.98632 = 552.3, rounded to 552 hp. Quote (Ferrari specification as printed by Just Cars): "Maximum power * 412 kW (560 cv) at 7500 rpm" (reproduced on a second request), footnote '* With 98 octane fuel'. CarShowroom's printed Ferrari table: 'Maximum power* | 412 kW (560 cv) @ 7500 rpm' (carshowroom-californiat). Evo's panel prints '553bhp @ 7500rpm' and KBB's US listing '553 hp @ 7500 RPM' (one horsepower apart by rounding). No separate SAE rating published by Ferrari for the US was found, so powerStandard is DIN PS.

weightLb.note: Ferrari's figure in pounds: 3,813 lb (1,730 kg). Quote (Ferrari specification table as printed by CarShowroom, Marc Greig, 18 June 2014): "Kerb weight** | 3813 lb", beside "Dry weight** | 3582 lb", footnote "** With lightweight optional equipment" (reproduced on a second request). The same table supplies the power and transmission entries. KBB's US listing for the 2018 California T Convertible 2D shows a curb weight of '3813 lbs.' (kbb-california); its 2015 page shows '3582 lbs.' (kbb-california-2015), the dry figure. Ferrari's dry weight is 1,625 kg (justcars-californiat: "Dry weight** 1625 kg", footnote "** With lightweight optional equipment"; Asphalte.ch: 'Dry weight is claimed at 1625kg'); the kerb figure is exactly 105 kg above it. Top Gear's auto-filled spec page prints 'Minimum Kerbweight: 1,625kg' (topgear-californiat-spec), the dry number. Step 3 of the weight order: Ferrari's kerb weight for a car with lightweight optional equipment; no standard-car curb weight was found, and a standard car is somewhat heavier. Folding hard-top 2+2 with the 7-speed dual-clutch gearbox (the only configuration).

discrepancies.reason: Dry vs kerb. Ferrari's specification gives both; the kerb figure is 105 kg above the dry one. KBB's 2015 page shows the dry figure (3,582 lb) as curb weight, its 2018 page the kerb figure (3,813 lb).
discrepancies.resolution: Used the kerb figure under weight step 3 (an optioned car's curb weight), since a curb weight ranks above a dry weight.
